newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ankara demands allied cover for Iraq's Turkomans.
newsitem.headline: Ankara demands allied cover for Iraq's Turkomans.

text.p: Turkey's foreign minister, in her latest round of consultations with the U.S. ambassador on events in neighbouring Iraq, on Saturday demanded Western protection for ethnic Turks in northern Iraq.

"Under Operation Provide Comfort it was envisaged that Kurdish citizens in northern Iraq be protected. We want the Turkomans to be taken within this framework of protection," Tansu Ciller told reporters after meeting ambassador Marc Grossman.
U.S.-led air patrols over northern Iraq -- known as Operation Provide Comfort -- were set up after the 1991 Gulf War to protect Iraqi Kurds from attacks by Baghdad.

Iraqi opposition sources and representatives of the Turkomans, a Turkic community of around two million of whom 200,000 live in northern Iraq, have said that Iraqi soldiers were arresting and killing some Turkomans after they stormed the main northern city of Arbil in a joint attack with an Iraqi Kurdish faction a week ago.
Officials of the Iraqi Turkoman Party have said around 2,000 Turkomans are missing from Arbil since Saturday's attack.
"The Turkomans are being harmed. They are suffering loss of life and loss of property," Ciller said.

Saturday's session was at least the third meeting between Ciller and Grossman this week and took place amid indications that Turkey would mount a strike against the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels across the border.

Turkish troops have been massing along the border with northern Iraq in apparent readiness to push against the PKK, but army officials would not confirm or deny Turkish press reports that troops had already mounted some cross-border attacks.
Residents of the border regions said some Turkish troops had gone to the western sector of the Turkey-Iraq frontier around Hezil stream in Uludere district.

"An advance group of around 300-400 special forces have entered the border area to clear PKK mines," one resident told Reuters. It was not clear if the forces crossed over the border or if the mine-clearing would be followed by attacks.
There was no sign of any incursion on Saturday, Reuters reporters in the region said.
Ciller said the Turkomans should have more of a say in what goes on in northern Iraq.

"The contribution of the Turkomans in the resolution of issues has become a necessity," she said. She did not say what form their contribution could take or how the allied forces' mandate would need to be changed to accommodate the Turkomans.

The United States said on Thursday it did not object to a Turkish plan to establish a three to six mile (five to 10 km) wide security zone in northern Iraq after Ankara said it would be temporary and not involve the stationing of Turkish troops.
France has opposed the Turkish plan and Russia has said it would destabilise the region further.

Turkey says the PKK has increased activity in the volatile border region since Baghdad intervened in fighting between Iraqi Kurd rebels in northern Iraq and Washington fired cruise missiles at targets in southern Iraqi in retaliation.
